about: Which macOS and Windows source files do the same job. scripts/parity-guard.py fails a change that touches one side of a group and none of the other, unless the pull request or a commit message has a line 'Parity: <reason>'. Every .swift file under mac/Sources and every .cs file directly in windows/ must appear here: in a group, or in macOnly / windowsOnly with the reason. A file may be in several groups; a change to it is matched when any file on the other side of any of its groups changed too.

groups.name: brightness rules, sun, Home Assistant template
config file: model, reading, saving, tuning
app shell: menu-bar / tray item, startup
monitor I/O, idle time, power source

macOnly.mac/Sources/DaylitCore/AccessibilityProm: macOS needs the Accessibility permission for the brightness keys; Windows needs none
macOnly.mac/Sources/DaylitCore/ConfigLocation.sw: the iCloud Drive config location and its last-good reload; Windows has one %APPDATA% path
macOnly.mac/Sources/DaylitCore/DDCTool.swift: which m1ddc program may run; Windows talks DDC/CI through Win32 directly
macOnly.mac/Sources/DaylitCore/LocalNetwork.swif: macOS's Local Network permission; Windows has no such permission
macOnly.mac/Sources/Daylit/LocalNetworkProbe.swi: macOS's Local Network permission; Windows has no such permission
a synced iCloud config can change the address on another Mac; the Windows config is never synced
macOnly.mac/Sources/DaylitCore/TokenKeychain.swi: moving the token to a keychain item only Daylit can read; Windows Credential Manager has no per-app items
macOnly.mac/Sources/Daylit/Demo.swift: scripted panel demo for README recordings, made on the Mac
